# Expert New Minor Forcing Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add an Expert-only New Minor Forcing auction after 1m–1M–1NT to find a three-card major fit or a four-card side major.

**Architecture:** Keep the convention in `packages/bots/src/player.ts` alongside existing auction continuations, recognizing only uncontested auctions generated by Expert bots. Cover responder asks, opener replies, and responder placement with focused tests.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Vitest, pnpm workspace.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-expert-new-minor-forcing.md`

## Global Constraints

- Keep `packages/core` platform-neutral.
- Preserve SAYC's natural, nonforcing new-suit continuations after opener's 1NT rebid.
- Use existing auction and hand APIs; do not add dependencies.

## Review Focus

- SAYC and Intermediate auctions must not gain the Expert artificial ask: test style gating.
- Either minor opening must identify the other minor as the ask: test both opening minors.
- Opener must prefer three-card support, then show a four-card other major, then deny both: test all replies.
- Responder must place game with a fit and invite or sign off appropriately after a denial: test placement.
- Competitive auctions must not trigger NMF: test an opponent intervention.

## Sources

- ACBL, [New Minor Forcing](https://web2.acbl.org/documentLibrary/play/Conventional-Wisdom/Conventional-Wisdom-All.pdf), describes the unbid minor ask after 1m–1M–1NT and opener's major-fit replies.
- ACBL SAYC booklet, [SAYC System Booklet](https://web2.acbl.org/documentlibrary/play/sayc_book.pdf), says new suits after a 1NT rebid are nonforcing; NMF therefore stays Expert-only.
